Must have:
- Self-hosted web application for a community seed library
- Reads a photo of a seed packet with OCR and records the variety and harvest year
- Records germination test results for each batch of seeds
- Emails the members who borrowed a variety when its germination rate falls below a set threshold
Nice to have:
- Suggests which varieties should be grown out again this season
- Prints labels for repackaged seeds

results.finalText:
Verdict: base growstuff/growstuff

Growstuff is the only mature, active, self-hosted project in this space: 475★, 79 contributors, releases through Oct 2026, and it already contains a seed library, packet-photo OCR, variety/harvest/batch fields, member accounts, and seed claims. It does not have germination tests, low-germination alerts, grow-out suggestions, or label printing, so it is a foundation to extend rather than a drop-in fit. Domain-specific seed-library repos I found are abandoned, unlicensed, or one-person prototypes.

**growstuff/growstuff — recommended base**
- Pros, confirmed in code: `app/controllers/seeds_controller.rb` implements a real seed-library catalogue with grouping by crop, source, harvest year, and use-by year; `app/models/stall.rb`, `stall_seed.rb`, and `claim.rb` implement members offering packets and others claiming them. `Seed` has `variety`, `batch_number`, `saved_at` (labelled “When were the seeds harvested/saved?”), `plant_before`, `quantity`, and `germination_days_min/max`.
- OCR is genuinely implemented: `script/ocr/read_packets.py` fetches packet front/back photos awaiting OCR, runs Tesseract (or another command), and stores `ocr-text`, engine, and timestamp; `Photo` has `ocr_text` and an `awaiting_ocr` scope.
- Cons: OCR only stores raw text; it does not extract variety or harvest year into the seed record. There is no germination-test model or result storage — `germination_days_*` is packet sowing information, not a test. A `Claim` is an immediate giveaway/swap (“theirs straight away”), not a loan with a return record. `NotifierMailer` only sends planting reminders, harvest reminders, and crop-request mail — no low-germination alert. No grow-out recommendation or label printing.
- Also note: it models peer-to-peer member stalls, not a librarian-managed central inventory. AGPL-3.0 is fine for self-hosting, but a modified network service must offer its source to users.

**juntagrico/juntagrico — ruled out**
- Pros: active, 55★, LGPL, mature community-garden/cooperative management: members, subscriptions, shares, deliveries, jobs, and mail templates (`juntagrico/entity/mailing.py`).
- Cons: the entity list (`member`, `subs`, `share`, `delivery`, `jobs`, `mailing`, etc.) contains no seeds, batches, germination, or loans. It would require building the entire seed domain.

**germinateplatform/germinate-vue — ruled out**
- Pros: active, Apache-2.0, genebank/genetic-resource UI with germplasm, trials, genotypes, pedigrees, and geography pages; `src/pages/data/germplasm/index.vue` is a germplasm browser.
- Cons: a research genebank database, not a member-facing lending library. No borrowing/claims, packet OCR, or threshold email; it is also only the frontend to a separate server.

**MultiMote/niimblue — component for the label-printing nice-to-have**
- Pros: 821★, MIT, active; browser-based label designer, print preview, and printer connector (`src/components/PrinterConnector.svelte`, `LabelDesigner.svelte`, `PrintPreview.svelte`) using Web Bluetooth/USB.
- Cons: standalone label printer app; no seed data model, members, OCR, germination tests, or email. Useful only for the repackaging-label requirement.

**Small seed-library projects — ruled out**
- `grimsbypl/seed-library` (2012, no licence), `Dalhousie-Libraries/Seed-Library` (2015, no licence), `Paperpotato/National-Seed-Library` (2021, no licence), and `mariostg/seed-library` (0★, unlicensed, very new) are domain-fit but fail on licence, adoption, and/or maintenance. `openfarmcc/OpenFarm` is archived.
